claim.level: Confirmed proximate bottleneck in the traced failing Night sample window. Individual optical primitive remains unassigned.
claim.mechanism: SoftwareRenderer CPU composition dominates; 17 complete Display::DrawAndSwap slices have 23.767 ms median CPU and 405.908 ms total CPU in 459.856 ms, compared with 17.734 ms whole-window main CPU and 0.248 ms median callback wall time.
claim.limits: The trace is a separate diagnostic after the untraced original failure, using its identical sampler with two marks. Both reproduce Night 33.3 ms; tracing overhead remains. This does not establish a universal failure rate, a specific Chromium defect or a native Android cause.

medianBoundary: Traced Day and Night have the same 25.488235294 ms mean callback interval; Day has 8/17 intervals over 21 ms and passes median 16.7 ms; Night has 9/17 and fails median 33.3 ms. This is a property of these raw samples; the original threshold and sampler remain unchanged.

androidSeparation.finding: APP_URL_BASE uses entry=android-handoff; bootstrap selects android-handoff.js and bypasses Day/Night. WebView/emulator internals still require their own investigation.
androidSeparation.deliveryVerification: PASS in both job logs; current pinned binary archives not re-analysed.
androidSeparation.originalSmokeStatus: FAIL job; precise native state not decoded in this follow-up.

sourceReference.scope: Primary code corroborates SoftwareRenderer tile/render-pass/filter CPU path; code alone does not assign per-element cost in this trace.

coveredWorkExperiment.verdict: REJECT AS REPAIR: small changes overlap local run variation; no reproducible sufficient CPU reduction. All eight local sample medians passed in both conditions, so pass counts cannot establish a repair. No product change retained. Appearance testing and further CI candidate runs were not undertaken after the cost discriminator failed.
